summary: FIXED (F4) and PROVEN: after the patch a verified note always has exactly the content the human had read when clicking Promote. Bounded: Notes={n1,n2}, MaxVer=2 (847 states, depth 14) and Notes={n1,n2,n3}, MaxVer=3 (105,648 states, depth 22). Unbounded: Lean 4 theorem ReviewGate.verified_is_what_was_read for any set of drafts, any contents, any trace length (0 sorry, axioms: propext only). Holds for clients that send the digest (the Hub UI does); a Promote request without `digest` is not checked.

modeled: Review page: 내용 읽기 (GET /api/notes/<path>) and Promote click
HubService.promote() reading the draft at promote time
any writer replacing the draft (skill, MCP write_draft, editor)
abstracted: A1 content = a version number; equal digest iff equal content (sha256[:16] collisions not modeled)
A2 promote is one atomic step (real: read → check → write dest → unlink; a write between read and unlink is lost, P3 still holds)
A3 body and digest come from the same bytes (service.py note())
A4 the browser echoes the digest it was given
A5 other promote refusals (frontmatter, Domain, dest exists) and the git commit are omitted
out_of_scope: Promote requests without `digest` (optional field; making it mandatory is a public-API decision)
apply_patch digest covers the patch file only, not the target note (recorded as candidate)

properties.meaning: P3 for every number of drafts, every content, every interleaving and trace length (inductive invariant: init_inv + step_inv)

findings.title: Promote verifies whatever is in the draft file at click time, not what the human read: a draft rewritten after '내용 읽기' becomes verified unread
findings.story: Brian opens a draft in the Review Gate and reads it. Before he clicks Promote, a Claude Code skill (or the MCP write_draft tool, or Obsidian) rewrites that file in 00_Inbox/ai-drafts. The click arrives; the Hub reads the file as it is now, sets status verified / reviewed today / origin mixed, moves it to 10_Domains and commits '[myelin:review] promote'. The note is recorded as human-reviewed, but nobody read that text. apply_patch already guards this with a digest; promote did not.

fix.summary: GET /api/notes/<path> returns `digest` (sha256[:16] of the file bytes) computed from the same bytes as the body. The Review page keeps it and sends it with the Promote click. promote() reads the draft once, refuses with 409 when the digest differs (nothing moved, nothing committed), and parses/promotes exactly the bytes it checked. On 409 the page closes the body so it has to be read again. `digest` is optional on the API (same policy as apply_patch).
